senses: you (informal, as opposed to courteous 您)
你:ni3.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 你 (nǐ, "you") has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two distinct, substantive entries sharing the identical key 你/ni3 — 你 ("you, informal, as opposed to courteous 您") and 妳 ("you [used for females in Taiwan; not commonly used in mainland China per CC-CEDICT's own note]") — and the pipeline correctly refuses to guess between them (data-pipeline.md §5.2). Adjudication: 你 is the intended candidate — it is the standard, gender-neutral form used for everyone in mainland Mandarin (the actual HSK-1 target), whereas 妳 is a Taiwan-specific, female-only variant CC-CEDICT itself flags as uncommon. Content is copied from the 你/你/ni3 CC-CEDICT entry verbatim, with its own "您[nin2]" cross-reference bracket manually normalised to display "您" only (data-pipeline.md §3/DEC-023's own rule, applied by hand since this override text does not pass through pipeline/cedict.ts's parser).

senses: (joining two nouns) and; together with; with (Taiwan pr. [han4])
和:he2.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 和 (hé, "and") — the single most essential HSK-1 sense of this headword — has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two entries sharing the identical key 和/he2 — the real word 和 (and/with/sum/to make peace/to draw/harmonious/Japan) and 龢 ("(literary) harmonious (variant of 和)", an archaic character variant). The pipeline's cross-reference classifier does not recognise 龢's sense as a pure pointer (the phrase "variant of X" is embedded mid-sentence rather than leading the sense), so it is misclassified as a second substantive entry, producing a conflicting-entries gap on the deck's most important still-missing word. Adjudication: 和 (the real, everyday word) is obviously intended; 龢 is an archaic character variant of no relevance to a beginner. Content copied verbatim from the 和/和/he2 CC-CEDICT entry; the "(Taiwan pr. [han4])" bracket is left in raw form deliberately — it is a pronunciation-variant annotation (not a cross-reference), which pipeline/sense-annotations.ts already converts to diacritic form for every other card post-override (see the already-shipped 会:hui4 card's "Taiwan pr. huǐ" for the identical, already-verified transform).

回:hui2.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 回 (huí, "to return") has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two substantive entries sharing the key 回/hui2 — the everyday word 回 (to go back/return, classifier for chapters/occurrences) and 迴 ("to curve; to return; to revolve", a literary/classical usage as in 迂回, 巡回). A third entry, 逥 ("variant of 迴"), is correctly excluded automatically as cross-reference-only. Adjudication: 回 (the everyday word — 回家, 回来, and the classifier uses) is obviously the HSK-1 intent; 迴's literary sense is not beginner vocabulary. 家:jia1.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 家 (jiā, "home/family") — one of the most basic HSK-1 words — has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two entries sharing the key 家/jia1 — the everyday word 家 (home/family/...) and 傢 ("used in 傢伙|家伙 and 傢俱|家俱", a bound form with no independent meaning). Adjudication: 家 is obviously intended; 傢 is not an independent word. Content and classifier (个) copied verbatim from the 家/家/jia1 CC-CEDICT entry.

里:li3.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 里 (lǐ, "inside") — the ubiquitous HSK-1 locative suffix (这里, 教室里 etc.) — has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two distinct, substantive entries sharing the key 里/li3 (already flagged as a real, unresolved defect by DEC-024's own consequences note) — 裡 ("lining/interior/inside/internal/also written 裏|里") and 里 ("li, ancient measure of length ~500m; neighborhood; administrative unit"). Adjudication: 裡's sense is the intended one — it is the everyday locative word every beginner needs (这里 "here", 家里 "at home"); the distance-unit 里 is specialised/historical vocabulary, not HSK-1. Content adapted from the 裡/里/li3 CC-CEDICT entry: the three near-synonymous top-level senses "interior/inside/internal" are merged into one array item for clarity (no meaning lost — they are the same core sense, not three distinct meanings), and the self-referential "also written 裏|里[li3]" clause is dropped entirely, since normalising it per DEC-023's own trad|simp rule would produce the circular, confusing statement "also written 里" (naming the headword itself).

岁:sui4.note: NOT YET FUNCTIONAL — see LR-002 Findings. 岁 (suì, the age classifier — 五岁 "five years old" — a core HSK-1 word) has no card at all: CC-CEDICT has two entries sharing the key 岁/sui4 — 嵗 ("variant of 歲|岁, year; years old", an archaic character variant) and 歲 ("classifier for years (of age); year; year (of crop harvests)").
